record.paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
record.original_question: For globally naked singularities produced as possible gravitational-collapse endstates, where no horizon prevents null or light rays from reaching future null infinity, what determines whether the exposed singularity is point-like or spatially extended, given the dependence on the matter fields and equation of state of the collapse model?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spherically symmetric gravitational collapse of a matter cloud in classical general relativity, modeled by a spacetime $(M,g)$ with stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ satisfying an equation of state relating pressure and density (e.g., $p=\alpha\rho$ with $\alpha\in(0,1/3]$, or more general barotropic relations). Assume the collapse terminates in a curvature singularity $S$ at a finite comoving time. The singularity $S$ is called globally naked if there exist future-directed causal (null or timelike) geodesics emanating from $S$ that reach future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$, i.e., no event horizon censors $S$ from distant observers.

Define $S$ to be point-like (event-like) if the set of points of $S$ from which future-directed null geodesics escape to $\mathscr{I}^+$ consists of a single spacetime event, and spatially extended (object-like) if this set contains a non-degenerate spacelike or null portion (a continuous one-parameter family of escaping events).

Problem: Within a general class of spherically symmetric collapse models (e.g., generalized Vaidya, inhomogeneous dust, or perfect-fluid clouds with equation of state $p=p(\rho)$), determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the initial data — the mass profile $m(r)$, the velocity profile $v(r)$, and the equation of state — that distinguish whether the resulting globally naked singularity is point-like or spatially extended. In particular, characterize the dependence of the dimensionality and causal structure of the visible portion of $S$ on the matter fields and the equation of state.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of when a globally naked singularity arising as the endstate of spherically symmetric gravitational collapse is point-like versus spatially extended remains an active research question. Numerous recent works (e.g., on generalized Vaidya spacetimes, dust collapse with various mass/velocity profiles, and perfect fluids with linear equation of state $p=\alpha\rho$) provide model-by-model conditions distinguishing the two cases, but no complete general criterion in terms of matter content and equation of state is established.

status_evidence.title: Globally visible singularity in an astrophysical setup
status_evidence.snippet: A collapsing dust cloud can give a globally visible singularity as its end state for certain mass profiles and velocity profiles.
status_evidence.claim: Specific mass and velocity profiles in dust collapse yield globally visible singularities, but a complete classification of point-like vs extended cases is not given.

status_evidence.title: Naked singularity formation in generalized Vaidya space-time
status_evidence.snippet: event-like naked singularity forms as endstate ... object-like visible singularities
status_evidence.claim: Two types of singularities (event-like vs object-like) are distinguished, indicating the structural question is still being investigated case by case.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational collapse and naked singularities
status_evidence.snippet: end state of gravitational collapse depends on the mass function, equation of state P=αρ
status_evidence.claim: The endstate's character depends on equation of state and mass function; a unified characterization remains incomplete.
